title: MoEngage reports unauthorised access to part of its cloud infrastructure via a compromised third-party vendor account
date_note: Date is Inc42's publication day; the article says MoEngage claims it identified and contained the incident in late October. No disclosure date is given.
geo_basis: headquarters as stated by Inc42 (Bengaluru and San Francisco)
summary: Inc42 reports that MoEngage, a SaaS company, suffered unauthorised access to a limited part of its cloud infrastructure through a compromised third-party vendor account. MoEngage says it contained the incident in late October and that less than 1% of customer accounts were affected, each notified. Analytics Insight reports that customer ZebPay told users contact, device, online data and recent account activity were exposed, and that its own servers and funds were not affected.
plain: A marketing software company says someone got into part of its cloud systems through a vendor's account. It says less than 1% of customer accounts were affected and they were told. ZebPay says some user details were exposed.
exec: A supplier-account compromise at a SaaS vendor reached customer accounts, and one customer, ZebPay, says user contact and activity data were exposed.
action: If you are a MoEngage customer, check for MoEngage's direct notice, and ask it what was affected in your account; ZebPay users should read ZebPay's notice.

evidence.quote: On November 21, the startup said that less than 1% of its customer accounts were affected.

validation.note: Inc42 and Analytics Insight both relay MoEngage's statement (Analytics Insight on 22 Nov, after Inc42); treated as one chain, not independent. No MoEngage notice read.

review.note: Compared title, summary, date_note, fewer-than-1% figure, late-October containment, ET nearly-seven-days claim and Bengaluru/San Francisco HQ against the Inc42 article of 21 Nov; single-source status is correct
